--- title: "Data" subtitle: "Where the shade map comes from, and who we follow home." jupyter: python3 --- ## Sources All inputs are public data. | Layer | Source | Used for | | --- | --- | --- | | Airborne LiDAR, March 2022 | City of Philadelphia, via NOAA Digital Coast and PASDA | ground, building and tree heights at 1 m | | Building footprints | City of Philadelphia (OpenDataPhilly) | building outlines | | Land cover 2018 | PASDA | tree canopy | | Canopy height (CHMv2) | Meta / WRI, CC BY 4.0 | trees just outside the city | | Pedestrian network | DVRPC | sidewalks and crosswalks | | OpenStreetMap | OSM contributors, ODbL | bridges, covered walkways, campus footways | | Transit | SEPTA, fall 2026 timetable | rapid-transit stations and frequent bus stops | | Properties | City of Philadelphia (OPA) | residential parcels, where walks end | ## The shade map ::: {.stat-row}
7,237 km

::: Building and tree heights come from the 2022 LiDAR survey, flown before the leaves came out. Building heights agree closely with the city's own records (median absolute difference 0.5 m over 541,222 buildings); bridges and elevated rail lines are included, so they cast shadows too. Trees cover 17% of the city in the model (the median tree is 15 m tall). Covered walkways and passages through buildings (4.2 km) are always in shade. ::: {#70cfe145 .cell .figure-light execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ![University City in the height model: buildings (blue and pink), bridges and other structures (orange) and trees (green).](data_files/figure-html/cell-5-output-1.jpeg){} ::: ::: ## Whose walks Each walk starts at a stop: any rapid-transit station (Regional Rail, L (Market-Frankford), B (Broad Street) or the T trolley tunnel) or a bus stop with at least 6 buses an hour in one direction between 15:00 and 19:00. Every home within 1.2 km walking distance of such a stop is one walk, 431,100 in all. The other 91,649 homes (17.5%), mostly in the Northeast and Roxborough, have no frequent stop that close. ::: {#8e55ddba .cell .figure-light execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ![Homes without a frequent stop within 1.2 km (red).](data_files/figure-html/cell-7-output-1.jpeg){width=640} ::: ::: ## University City For University City we mapped the entrances and indoor passages of 41 buildings (4.4 km of passages); 10 of them can be entered without a Penn ID. Campus footpaths from OpenStreetMap are added to the sidewalk network there. ## Known gaps - Outside University City, campus and park paths are missing, so cooler options inside campuses and parks are understated. - Shadows assume clear skies on two summer days; trees are mapped from leaf-off LiDAR and 2018 land cover, buildings from 2022. - Missing or misplaced footprints, newer buildings and temporary objects (parked trains, scaffolding) affect shade locally. - The timetable is one weekday in fall 2026; summer service may differ.
